diasporaWeek.heroImageAlt: Panoramic skyline of Hargeisa at dusk
diasporaWeek.heroTheme: Internal Cohesion is the Key to Recognition
diasporaWeek.heroSubtitle: Reconnect with Somaliland, discover investment opportunities, experience our culture, and explore the best hotels, cafés, restaurants, attractions, and events across Hargeisa.
diasporaWeek.countdownEnded: Diaspora Week 2026 has concluded — thank you for joining us.
diasporaWeek.quickAccessAriaLabel: Quick access to hotels, restaurants, cafés, attractions and events
diasporaWeek.aboutBody1: Somaliland Diaspora Week brings sons and daughters of the nation home to Hargeisa — from Minneapolis to London, Nairobi to Dubai — for five days of reconnection, dialogue and celebration. It is a moment to stand together, share ideas and reaffirm a shared identity.
diasporaWeek.aboutBody2: This year's theme, "Internal Cohesion is the Key to Recognition," reflects a simple truth: unity at home is the foundation everything else is built on. Through cultural festivals, investment forums, youth panels and community town halls, Diaspora Week 2026 is about building that foundation together.
diasporaWeek.infoSubtitle: The essentials for Somaliland Diaspora Week 2026, at a glance.
diasporaWeek.infoDatesBody: Sunday 2 August through Thursday 6 August 2026 — five full days of programming.
diasporaWeek.infoLocationBody: Hargeisa, the capital of Somaliland, hosting venues across the city.
diasporaWeek.infoThemeBody: "Internal Cohesion is the Key to Recognition" — unity as the foundation for the nation's future.
diasporaWeek.infoAudienceBody: Every Somalilander abroad, their families, and friends of Somaliland everywhere.
diasporaWeek.highlightsSubtitle: A packed program of culture, business and community, open to every visitor.
diasporaWeek.highlight1Body: A grand welcome to open Diaspora Week, bringing together government, community leaders and returning families.
diasporaWeek.highlight2Body: Diaspora entrepreneurs and local businesses meet to explore partnerships and opportunities across Somaliland.
diasporaWeek.highlight3Body: Music, poetry, food and traditional dress celebrating the richness of Somaliland's culture.
diasporaWeek.highlight4Body: Young Somalilanders from home and abroad share ideas on technology, education and the road ahead.
diasporaWeek.highlight5Body: An evening of celebration honoring the contributions of the diaspora to Somaliland's growth.
diasporaWeek.highlight6Body: An open dialogue on internal cohesion — the theme at the heart of this year's Diaspora Week.
diasporaWeek.hotelsSubtitle: Comfortable stays near the action — book early, Hargeisa fills up fast during Diaspora Week.
diasporaWeek.restaurantsSubtitle: From traditional Somali cuisine to modern dining, right across the city.
diasporaWeek.cafesSubtitle: Reconnect with old friends and new over Hargeisa's best coffee.
diasporaWeek.attractionsSubtitle: Make the most of your visit with Hargeisa's landmarks and hidden gems.
diasporaWeek.mapSubtitle: The event hub, recommended hotels, restaurants, cafés and attractions — all in one map.
diasporaWeek.offersTitle: Special Offers for Diaspora Week Visitors
diasporaWeek.offersSubtitle: Limited-time offers from our partners across Hargeisa.
diasporaWeek.tipsSubtitle: A few essentials before you land in Hargeisa.
diasporaWeek.tip1Body: Most visitors can obtain a Somaliland visa on arrival at Hargeisa's Egal International Airport — check requirements for your passport before you travel.
diasporaWeek.tip2Body: The Somaliland shilling and US dollars are both widely accepted; mobile money (Zaad, eDahab) is the easiest way to pay locally.
diasporaWeek.tip3Body: Taxis and hotel transfers are the most convenient way to move between venues during Diaspora Week.
diasporaWeek.tip4Body: Light, modest clothing for warm days, something warmer for the evenings, and comfortable shoes for a full program.
diasporaWeek.faq1A: A five-day national gathering in Hargeisa welcoming Somalilanders from around the world home for culture, investment and dialogue, under the theme "Internal Cohesion is the Key to Recognition."
diasporaWeek.faq2A: Everyone — diaspora Somalilanders, their families, and anyone with an interest in Somaliland are welcome at every public event.
diasporaWeek.faq3Q: Do I need a visa to attend?
diasporaWeek.faq3A: Most visitors can get a Somaliland visa on arrival at Hargeisa's airport. Check the Travel Tips section above and the full Travel Guide for details specific to your passport.
diasporaWeek.faq4A: Accommodation isn't included — but the Recommended Hotels section above makes it easy to book a stay in Hargeisa for the week.
diasporaWeek.faq5Q: How do I get involved or find out more?
diasporaWeek.faq5A: Reach out through our Contact page — our team can point you to the right event, forum or venue for what you're looking for.
diasporaWeek.ctaSubtitle: Whether you're coming home or joining from afar, Somaliland Diaspora Week 2026 is for every son and daughter of this nation.

about.paragraph2: We work with local hotels, restaurants, guides and cultural institutions to keep our listings <highlight>accurate, current and genuinely useful</highlight>, whether you're planning a first visit or looking for a new favorite cafe close to home.
about.paragraph3: Have a business you'd like listed, or spotted something out of date? Reach out through our <link>contact page</link> — we'd love to hear from you.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Go Hargeisa ("we", "our") respects your privacy. This policy applies to both the Go Hargeisa website and the Go Hargeisa mobile app (Android and iOS), which share the same account and data — it explains what information we collect and how it is used.
privacy.infoItem1: Account information (name, email) when you sign up, either directly or via "Continue with Google".
privacy.infoItem2: Reviews, favorites, saved trips, and booking requests you create while signed in.
privacy.infoItem4: Basic usage analytics to help us improve the site and app.
privacy.infoItem5: On the mobile app only, a push-notification device token — if you enable notifications — used solely to deliver notices about your own bookings/account.
privacy.useText: We use your information solely to operate Go Hargeisa — personalizing your dashboard, sending the newsletter you opted into, notifying you about your bookings, and responding to contact form submissions. We do not sell personal data.
privacy.sharingText: We use Supabase to host our database, authentication, and file storage — your account and content data resides with them as our data processor, under their own security safeguards. If you sign in with "Continue with Google", Google processes that authentication on our behalf and shares your name/email with us as authorized by you. We do not sell, rent, or share your personal data with advertisers or other third parties.
privacy.retentionText: We keep your account data for as long as your account is active. You can permanently delete your account and all associated data (reviews, favorites, saved trips) at any time from Account Settings in your dashboard — no need to contact us. You can also request a copy of your data or ask us to correct it by emailing us.
privacy.childrenText: Go Hargeisa is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from them. If you believe a child has provided us with personal information, contact us and we will delete it.
privacy.mobileText: The Go Hargeisa app requests only the permissions it needs to function: internet access, network-status detection (to show an offline screen when needed), notification delivery (only if you enable it), and vibration (for interface feedback). The app does not access your camera, microphone, contacts, or precise location, and photo uploads (for reviews) use your device's own photo picker rather than any permission granted directly to the app.
privacy.securityText: We use industry-standard measures (encrypted connections, access-controlled databases) to protect your information, but no method of transmission or storage is 100% secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.
privacy.contactText: Questions about this policy, or requests to access/correct/delete your data, can be sent to info@gohargeisa.com.

travelGuide.title: Hargeisa Travel Guide
travelGuide.subtitle: Practical information to help you plan a smooth trip
travelGuide.infoSubtitle: From visas to safety tips, here's what to expect.
travelGuide.visaBody: Most nationalities can obtain a Somaliland visa on arrival at Egal International Airport (HGA), or in advance from a Somaliland representative office abroad. Bring two passport photos and pay the fee in USD.
travelGuide.airportBody: Egal International Airport (HGA) sits about 5 km from the city center. Taxis and hotel shuttles are available outside arrivals; agree on a fare before departing.
travelGuide.transportBody: Shared and private taxis are the main way to get around the city. Ride-hailing apps are limited, so hotels can arrange trusted drivers for day trips and airport transfers.
travelGuide.currencyBody: The Somaliland shilling (SLSH) is the local currency, though US dollars are widely accepted for hotels, larger purchases and taxis. Mobile money (Zaad, eDahab) is used everywhere, even in small shops.
travelGuide.safetyBody: Hargeisa is generally safe for visitors who take normal precautions. Dress modestly, avoid photographing government or military buildings, and check locally for the latest security guidance before travel.
travelGuide.emergencyBody: Police: 999 · Hargeisa Group Hospital: available via hotel front desk · Always keep your hotel's address and phone number with you.
travelGuide.internetBody: Local SIM cards (Telesom, Somtel) are inexpensive and easy to buy with a passport. Data coverage is solid in the city center; most hotels and cafes also offer WiFi.
travelGuide.customsBody: Somaliland is a conservative Muslim society. Dress modestly, greet with your right hand, and expect Friday to be a rest day for many businesses.
travelGuide.bestTimeBody: November to February offers the coolest, most comfortable weather. The rainy season (April–May) can make travel outside the city harder.
travelGuide.packingBody: Light, modest clothing (long sleeves and trousers/long skirts recommended), a scarf for women, comfortable walking shoes, sun protection, and a universal power adapter.
travelGuide.faq1Q: Do I need a visa to visit Hargeisa?
travelGuide.faq1A: Most travelers can get a Somaliland visa on arrival at the airport, though it's worth checking current requirements for your nationality before you fly.
travelGuide.faq2A: Hargeisa is considered one of the more stable and welcoming cities in the region, but as with any destination, it's wise to stay informed and use common-sense precautions.
travelGuide.faq3Q: What language is spoken in Hargeisa?
travelGuide.faq3A: Somali is the primary language, with Arabic and English also widely understood, especially in hotels and among younger residents.

transportation.title: Transportation
transportation.subtitle: How to move around Hargeisa comfortably and safely
transportation.airportTransfersBody: Egal International Airport (HGA) is roughly 5 km from downtown. Most hotels can arrange a pickup; airport taxis are also readily available.
transportation.taxisBody: The most common way to get around. Agree on the fare before you get in, or ask your hotel to book a trusted driver.
transportation.minibusesBody: Shared minibuses run fixed routes across the city and are the cheapest option, though schedules are informal.
transportation.rentalBody: Self-drive rentals are uncommon; most visitors hire a car with a driver for day trips outside the city, arranged through hotels or tour operators.

attractionsPage.whyVisitSubtitle: A city of resilience, hospitality and stories waiting to be discovered.
attractionsPage.whyHistoryBody: From the MiG Monument to colonial-era streets, Hargeisa's landmarks tell the story of Somaliland's journey to peace and independence.
attractionsPage.whyCultureBody: Experience Somali hospitality, traditional markets and a vibrant creative scene rooted in centuries of trade and tradition.
attractionsPage.whySafetyBody: Somaliland is known as one of the safest and most stable destinations in the Horn of Africa, with locals eager to welcome visitors.
attractionsPage.whyValueBody: Enjoy authentic experiences, food and stays at a fraction of the cost of better-known destinations.
attractionsPage.ctaSubtitle: Plan your stay and discover everything the city has to offer, from comfortable hotels to unforgettable meals.
